Optimal.Notes: A slight bump in GPU clock and TDP over MaxBattery to improve frame-time consistency; FSR at a slightly higher internal resolution gives better image clarity for spotting distant targets. View distance on Medium is important for situational awareness in a tactical game.

profiles.Summary: Squad is a demanding tactical FPS that pushes well beyond the Steam Deck's GPU class, with minimum PC specs already exceeding the Deck's GPU performance; expect 30 fps or below in busy 100-player servers even at low settings. The game is rated Playable on Steam Deck and runs via Proton Gold tier, but large battles, base building, and combined-arms chaos will stress the hardware significantly.
profiles.BasisNote: No Steam Deck-specific player reports were found; profiles are estimated from PC minimum requirements (which already exceed the Deck's GPU class) and Deck hardware capabilities. On first run, check fps in a real 100-player server — if it drops below 25 fps consistently, lower View Distance and Effects Quality further, and consider staying on smaller servers or training maps.

MaxBattery.Notes: Render at sub-native with FSR upscaling to ease GPU load; 8 W TDP and locked GPU clock keep thermals and battery drain low. Expect dips below 30 fps in the largest combined-arms engagements — this is the hardware ceiling.

KnownIssues: VAC (Valve Anti-Cheat) is enabled — some servers may block or kick Linux/Proton clients; verify server compatibility before joining
No native controller support for a complex tactical FPS; keyboard/mouse via Deck controls is awkward without a layout configured
Large 100-player battles with vehicles and base structures can cause significant frame drops well below 30 fps
Unreal Engine 4 shader compilation stutters may occur on first launch or when entering new areas

MaxPerformance.Notes: Full TDP and max GPU clock chase 40 fps on the 40 Hz refresh rate; the 40 fps cap prevents runaway power draw. Expect the cap to hold in lighter infantry-only skirmishes but drop to the high 20s during large vehicle battles — reduce View Distance to Low if stuttering becomes frequent.

Optimal.Notes: A 40 Hz refresh rate locked to 40 fps gives the smoothest pacing the Deck can reliably manage in Squad; FSR upscaling from ~1024x640 recovers enough GPU headroom for medium view distance. Expect drops into the low 30s during large-scale engagements.

profiles.Summary: Squad is a demanding tactical FPS that significantly exceeds the Steam Deck's GPU capabilities, with minimum specs calling for a GTX 1060 6GB — a step above what the Deck can offer — making stable framerates a real challenge even at low settings. The game is rated Playable on Steam Deck with a gold ProtonDB tier, but large 100-player battles with combined-arms combat will stress the hardware heavily, requiring aggressive resolution scaling and low settings to stay playable.

On first run, check framerates in an active 100-player server — if you see sustained drops below 25 fps even on Max Battery settings, the server population and map may simply be too demanding for the hardware.
